hyperfixation.title: Propositional interpretability
hyperfixation.body: Chalmers' thing is basically: the right unit of analysis for "what does a model believe" is propositions, not features or circuits. I'm not sure he's right, but it's the most honest frame anyone's offered. If you believe propositions are real, then mechinterp is closer to cognitive science than to compiler analysis, and Saklas-style steering is closer to persuasion than to patching.
